children: shares rose more than 3% in premarket trading on Tuesday after the Chinese tech giant gave further details on its Qwen artificial intelligence models and its full-stack AI infrastructure.

Speaking at its annual cloud conference, Alibaba Chairman Joe Tsai said AI has “continuously expanded our imagination of technological capabilities” and that it “possesses vast potential” in a wide range of real-world situations.
“This is the true meaning of ‘Intelligence Goes Beyond,' guiding AI from technological breakthroughs toward value creation,” Tsai said, referring to the conference's theme.
The company said its newest AI model, Qwen 4, is in training and that future models, the Qwen 4.5 and Qwen 5 model series, would scale up to 5 to 10T parameters.
The latest hot topic in the AI industry is recursive self-improvement, a process in which an AI system uses its own capabilities to design, code, and train its next successor, building upon itself.

Alibaba said its current flagship model, Qwen 3.8-Max, had completed 33 iterative cycles via RSI. The process took more than a month of automated runs, which spanned everything, including design, data validation, experimentation, and diagnosing errors.
In addition, Alibaba said the updated Qwen 3.8-Max was able to increase its Artificial Analysis score to 45 from 40 via RSI.

Alibaba also introduced several other new models on Tuesday, including Qwen3.8-LiveTranslate. This model is aimed at translation fidelity, fluency, and brevity and can reduce latency to 2.3 seconds from 2.8 seconds for better real-time translation.

It also took the wraps off Qwen-Audio-3.1-TTS-Next, an audio generation model that can create a complete cinematic soundscape, as well as new versions of Qwen-Audio-3.1-ASR (Automatic Speech Recognition), Qwen-Audio-3.1-TTS (Text-to-Speech), and Qwen-Audio-3.1-Realtime.
Alibaba also previewed its newest image generation model, Qwen-Image 3.1, set to be available later this year.
showed off its Zhenwu V900 AI chip on Tuesday, which it says is China's most powerful AI accelerator, as it looks to compete with offerings from Nvidia
The company also set a target of more than 20 GW of global data center capacity by 2032.

title: Alibaba rises as it gives further details on Qwen models, full-stack AI infrastructure
